executiveSummary.label: Business outlook
executiveSummary.text: Strong. Sales have compounded at about 14% a year over five years, operating margin has risen from 23% to 29%, and the company is almost debt-free. Order-book data is not in the supplied source, so forward visibility is unverified.

executiveSummary.label: Stock valuation
executiveSummary.text: Full. At 43.8x trailing earnings and 11.4x book, the market already prices in sustained high-teens growth. Profit growth in the latest trailing period has slowed.

executiveSummary.label: Risk-adjusted view

sections.title: 1. Business Quality and Sector Positioning
sections.content:
Reported facts
- The source classifies BEL as "Industrials" on NSE/BSE in India. It gives no segment, customer or
product breakdown.
- ROCE is 37% and ROE is 27.8%. These are high returns on capital.
- Operating margin (OPM) was 17% in Mar 2015 and 29% in Mar 2025, Mar 2026 and TTM.
- Borrowings are ₹65 Cr against ₹22,967 Cr of reserves.
- Promoter holding has been stable at 51.14% since Mar 2020.
Judgement: The numbers show a profitable, capital-efficient, essentially debt-free business. Sector
positioning, competitive moat, import substitution and customer concentration cannot be assessed
from the data. The investor should check the company's filings for these.

- Sales growth: 16.2% in FY26 and 17.3% in FY25. The five-year CAGR (Mar 2021 to Mar 2026) is
about 14.3%.
- Net profit growth: 14.4% in FY26, against 31.5% in FY25. The three-year CAGR (FY23 to FY26) is
about 26%, and the five-year CAGR is about 24%.
- Latest trend: TTM net profit of ₹6,128 Cr is only 1.3% above FY26's ₹6,048 Cr. TTM sales are
4.1% above FY26.
- Margin: TTM OPM of 29% is flat on FY26, so margin expansion has stalled.
- Depreciation: It rose from ₹436 Cr (FY25) to ₹524 Cr (FY26), and TTM is ₹564 Cr. This trims profit
growth.
- Other income: It peaked at ₹768 Cr in FY25 and is now about ₹590 Cr. That is roughly 7% of
profit before tax, so earnings are mostly operating.
Judgement: The five-year record is excellent. The most recent trailing data shows deceleration, and
the source has no quarterly breakdown to explain it. Quarterly results are the first thing the investor
should check.
Data caveat: The source lists "EPS 0.73" in key metrics. That is inconsistent with the annual EPS of
₹8.27 (FY26) and ₹8.38 (TTM). The reported P/E of 43.8 on a price of ₹368 implies EPS of about
₹8.40. I use the ₹8.38 TTM figure and treat 0.73 as a likely single-quarter or data-capture error.

The source's forensic check flags operating cash flow (₹1,494 Cr) at under 50% of net profit
(₹6,128 Cr).
Over FY22 to FY26, cumulative operating cash flow was about ₹11,847 Cr against cumulative
net profit of about ₹20,712 Cr, a conversion of roughly 57%.
Cash flow is lumpy, which is typical of project and defence working-capital cycles. But two weak
years in the last three (FY25 and FY26) mean the earnings are not yet turning into cash.
Free cash flow was negative in FY25.
Judgement: The balance sheet is financially strong with almost no leverage. The risk lies in working
capital, not debt. Dividends of about 30% of profit are being paid from a thin cash base.

sections.content:
Unavailable. The source contains no order-book value, order inflow, book-to-bill ratio, execution
timeline or management guidance. I will not estimate them.
What the source does show
- A news headline dated 27 Oct 2026 says defence stocks including Bharat Electronics rallied as the
Centre cleared ₹2.12 lakh crore of procurement proposals.
- This is a sector-level headline. The source does not say how much, if any, of this is allocated to
BEL, or when.
- The consistent 14% to 17% sales growth over the past several years is the only revenue evidence
in the data. It is a record, not a forecast.
What the investor should monitor
- Order book as a multiple of TTM sales (₹28,596 Cr)
- Quarterly order inflow
- Conversion of the cleared procurement proposals into actual BEL contracts
- Management's revenue and margin guidance

- Bear: Order conversion slips, working-capital strain continues and margin eases from 29%.
Foreign selling persists and the multiple compresses toward a lower-growth industrial multiple.
- Base: Sales growth is a little below the FY26 rate of 16%. This is consistent with the TTM profit
slowdown. Margins hold near 28.5% and the multiple drifts down modestly.

investors. A company growing profit at about 8% to 17% while trading at 43.8x can see its multiple
compress and offset the growth.

sections.title: 8. Growth Potential
sections.content:
Yes on business potential, with caveats.
- Evidence for: five-year sales CAGR of about 14%, margins up 6 percentage points over the
decade, ROCE of 37%, no debt, rising fixed assets (capacity being added), and a sector-level
headline of ₹2.12 lakh crore of procurement clearances.
- Evidence of caution: TTM profit is up only 1.3% on FY26, margin expansion has stalled at 29%,
and cash conversion is poor.
- The size of the future order book, the share of it that BEL wins, and the pace of execution are the
key unknowns. None is in the data.
Business potential: Positive. Expected stock return from ₹368 to mid-2027: Roughly flat, with a
wide spread.

sections.content:
Summary table
Dimension View
Business quality Strong, with high ROCE and ROE and almost no debt
Growth Healthy over five years, with the latest trailing data
slowing
Cash quality Weak, with a red flag on operating cash flow
Visibility Not verifiable from the supplied data
Valuation Full at 43.8x P/E
Technicals Data unavailable; price near the 52-week low
Scenario range to mid-2027 ₹227 to ₹486, probability-weighted about ₹355
Practical stances
Investor type Stance
Existing holders
Hold. The business is sound, but the expected return is
flat. Review if operating cash flow stays weak or the
price breaks ₹355 without a fundamental reason.
Fresh investors
Do not buy a full position at ₹368. Start small, or wait
for either a lower price or evidence of order conversion
and cash recovery.
Aggressive investors
A small tactical position near ₹355 to ₹368 is defensible
given the bull-case upside of up to about 32%. Use
₹355 as a stop and size for a possible 30% or larger
drawdown.
Conservative investors
Avoid new money for now. Wait for a better price or for
cash conversion to recover.
Best overall judgement: BEL is a high-quality business whose price already reflects that quality. At
₹368, the base case gives roughly flat returns and the bear case loses more than the bull case gains
in percentage terms (up to -38% against up to +32%). I would hold, not add, and treat sub-₹300
prices or a visible improvement in cash conversion and order data as the triggers to turn
constructive.

It is not financial advice or a recommendation to buy or sell. Scenarios are illustrative, not promises.
Consult a licensed adviser and verify all figures from company filings before investing.

Business potential versus stock return: The business can deliver growth and still disappoint
investors. A company growing profit at about 8% to 17% while trading at 43.8x can see its multiple
compress and offset the growth.

8. Does the company still have potential to grow?
Yes on business potential, with caveats.
- Evidence for: five-year sales CAGR of about 14%, margins up 6 percentage points over the
decade, ROCE of 37%, no debt, rising fixed assets (capacity being added), and a sector-level
headline of ₹2.12 lakh crore of procurement clearances.
- Evidence of caution: TTM profit is up only 1.3% on FY26, margin expansion has stalled at 29%,
and cash conversion is poor.
- The size of the future order book, the share of it that BEL wins, and the pace of execution are the
key unknowns. None is in the data.
Business potential: Positive. Expected stock return from ₹368 to mid-2027: Roughly flat, with a
wide spread.
